messages.subject: Announcement: Rhipe 0.67
messages.subject_clean: Announcement: Rhipe 0.67
messages.body_plain:
Greetings,

I am happy to announce that we have pushed out a new version of Rhipe
(0.67).  Various aspects of this version were contributed by Saptarshi
Guha, Jeremah Rounds (myself), and Ryan Hafen.  Saptarshi Guha asked
me to make the announcement.

It is available for download from here: https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/downloads

We are assembling version changes here:
https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/wiki/Version-History-and-Notes

The major goal of this version was something that the average user
would not notice which is that "R CMD check Rhipe_0.67.tar.gz" reports
no warnings or notes about the package; previously it would get quite
upset.  However in addition to meeting that goal, some quality of life
changes and bug fixes went into the new version.

= New rhoptions() =

rhoptions(zip= ...) and rhoptions(mapred=...) are now usable to set
defaults for all subsequent rhmr calls.  This is helpful in separating
out your cluster/location specific parameters from your job/task
specific parameters.

= New Job Monitoring =

The new function rhwatch() is now being engineered as the monitoring
function, so all these should work:
rhwatch(mr)
rhwatch(rhex(mr))
rhwatch("some_job_id")

= New HDFS Working Directories =

To help along portability, we also have hdfs.setwd() and hdfs.getwd()
which set paths to use as the base of subsequent relative paths.  For
example consider:
hdfs.setwd("/wsc/jrounds")
mr = rhmr(..., ifolder="data09.in <http://data09.in>", ofolder="data09.out")

This now means take the ifolder as /wsc/jrounds/data09.in <http://data09.in>  and take
the ofolder as /wsc/jrounds/data09.out, but this call continues to
have the same meaning it always had and does not use the HDFS working
directory.
mr = rhmr(..., ifolder="/data09.in <http://data09.in>", ofolder="/data09.out")

Those of you that test jobs on laptops or small clusters and then do
work on production clusters can use the new site specific rhoptions()
and hdfs.setwd to make your code easier to move around.

= Additionally =

Those people that build runners and Rhipe MapReduce archives  will
want to note that imperious.so has been renamed "RhipeMapReduce" to be
clearer to new users.  There is now an easy way to find the location
of this executable use: rhoptions()$RhipeMapReduce.  You should only
need to rewrite your scripts to make use of the new RhipeMapReduce
where previously they used imperious.so to use the new executable.

I have an experimental function called "bashRhipeArchive".  If the
user is using a bash shell it outputs a copy of a usable archive to
the current R working directory and places a copy of that archive on
the HDFS at the current HDFS working directory.  If it works right
there is nothing else the user needs to do, and it reports the new
rhoptions() to make use of the archive for running MapReduce jobs, but
it is experimental.

Also, there are number changes that Saptarshi worked on such as
default tmp directories for certain calls.  In addition to streaming
lining a couple of use cases such as rhmr now defaults to
inout=c("lapply","sequence") when N  is not NA.

= Thanks =

Thanks for using Rhipe.  Let us know if there is anything we can help
you with.

Jeremiah

With regards to this: when ofolder is missing in rhmr, the rhmr function creates a folder in the
HDFS folder rhabsolute.hdfs.path(rhoptions()$HADOOP.TMP.FOLDER) (which needs to be set manually, else it is NA)
the file created can be found in rhmr(..)[[1]]$rhipe_output_folder.  Example

rhwatch(z<- rhmr(map=map,reduce=NA, inout=c(NA,'seq'),jarfiles="/user/sguha/tmp/rhipecrashreport.jar",mapred=mapred),read=FALSE)

1. reduce=NA implies mapred.reduce.tasks=0
2. rhwatch will start and monitor the job, and will not read the results back in (read=FALSE, by default read=TRUE)
3. the output is stored in z[[1]]$rhipe_output_folder (e.g.

> z[[1]]$rhipe_output_folder
[1] "/user/sguha/tmp/rhipe-temp-de755b0879eb590498345b53532caa86/"

)
4. From ?rhwatch
If the state is SUCCEEDED and total output size (in MB) is less
     than ‘rhoptions()$max.read.in.size’ the data is read with a
     warning if the number of records is more than
     ‘rhoptions()$reduce.output.records.warn’. If
     ‘rhoptions()$rhmr.max.records.to.read.in <http://rhmr.max.records.to.read.in>’ is not NA, that many
     records is read. This only works for Sequence output.

5. others, incase the user is not aware
rhoptions()$templates$scalarsummer is a summer reducer (e.g. wordcount) and be given to reduce in rhmr
rhoptions()$templates$colsummer is a column summer (in rhcollect, pass a matrix as the value, it's columns will be summed)

To echo Jeremiah, thanks for using RHIPE. If you have requests or issues, post here or submit to github.

Cheers
Saptarshi

Is it possible to accomplish the same with Rhipe? How to build Rhipe to make it ship local R archive to compute nodes?

--Konstantin

I put an experimental function into 0.67 called bashRhipeArchive.  I made it for my coworkers at Purdue. It is experimental because it is difficult to build these things in a portable fashion.  Between all the flavors of linux, shells, file systems, hadoop it is quite a challenge to figure out how to write one script for everyone.   I have the hope that it would work on most bash shells, but I don't know.

It doesn't create archives with the same directory structure or runner scripts that Saptarshi uses.  I basically copy R's home directory and copy all the shared libraries to the lib directory of that folder.    The runner script itself is found in <R copy>/library/Rhipe/bin/RhipeMapReduce.sh.  The contents of the script can be seen here: https://github.com/saptarshiguha/RHIPE/blob/Rhipe_0.67/code/R/inst/bin/RhipeMapReduce.sh

After rhinit() to use it you need to setwd() to somewhere you can write to on linux and hdfs.setwd() to somewhere you can write to on the hdfs.  Then you call bashRhipeArchive()  If everything works it will report your new zips options and runner options to use in the future.  There is a lot of reasons it might not work though. I tested it on three hadoop clusters, but not extensively.

Is that correct that Rhipe's runner "rhoptions(runner=..." runs in it's own environments and can not get them from mapred.child.env?

If so what prevents passing environments set in mapred.child.env to the runner? Then there will be no need for runner running a script - this will make debugging much easier. Why not just call:
config <- list(
mapred.child.env="R_HOME=./Rfolder/Rdist/R,R_HOME_DIR=./Rfolder/Rdist/R,PATH=./Rfolder/Rdist/R/bin:./Rfolder/Rdist:${PATH},LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./Rfolder/Rdist:./Rfolder/Rdist/R/lib:/usr/lib64:.:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"

rhoptions(runner="RhipeMapReduce --slave --silent --vanilla --max-ppsize=100000 --max-nsize=1G")

Excellent! I made a modification to the environment variables given RhipeMapReduce (Hadoop does variable
substitution  and fails with PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH, the fix i pushed is not to perform substitution on PATH, LD...)

source("~/prefix.rhipe.code.R")
m <- ewrap({
  rhcollect(1,1)
})
mapred <- list(R_HOME="./Rfolder-release/Rdist/R"
               ,R_HOME_DIR="./Rfolder-release/Rdist/R"
               ,PATH="./Rfolder-release/Rdist:./Rfolder-release/Rdist/R/bin:${PATH}"
               ,LD_LIBRARY_PATH="./Rfolder-release/Rdist:./Rfolder-release/Rdist/R/lib:/usr/lib64:.:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}"
               ,mapreduce.map.maxattempts=1)
rhoptions(runner="./Rfolder-release/Rdist/RhipeMapReduce --slave --silent --vanilla --max-ppsize=100000 --max-nsize=1G")
f <- rhwatch(rhmr(map=m,N=100,reduce=NA,mapred=mapred))

where prefix.rhipe.code.R can be found here :  http://sguha.pastebin.mozilla.org/1604073

I'll test this a bit more before updating the wiki.

Thanks and Regards
Saptarshi

Trailing ${PATH} and ${LD_LIBRARY_PATH} are actually not needed, here is the final template that works for me for a few tests:
#! /usr/bin/env Rscript
library(Rhipe)
rhinit(TRUE,TRUE,buglevel=2000)
mapred <- list(
   mapreduce.map.maxattempts=1,
   R_HOME="./Rfolder/Rdist/R",
   R_HOME_DIR="./Rfolder/Rdist/R",
   PATH="./Rfolder/Rdist/R/bin:./Rfolder/Rdist",
   LD_LIBRARY_PATH="./Rfolder/Rdist:./Rfolder/Rdist/R/lib:/usr/lib64"
)
options <- rhoptions()
options$runner[1] <- "./Rfolder/Rdist/RhipeMapReduce --slave --silent --vanilla --max-ppsize=100000 --max-nsize=1G"
map <- expression(...)
reduce <- expression(...)
inputdir <- ...
outputdir <- ...
job <- rhmr(
  jobname  = "Runing Rhipe on a cluster without R"
  map      = map,
  reduce   = reduce,
  mapred   = mapred,
  ifolder  = inputdir,
  ofolder  = outputdir,
  inout    = c("text", "text"),
  opt      = options,
  zips     = "/user/kshmakov/Rfolder.tar.gz"
)
rhex(job)

Archive Rfolder.tar.gz contains original R script without substitution.

A few tweaks:
1) when mapreduce.map.maxattempts=1 not set and default value 4 is used 3 attempts usually fail (with code 139) for 1-mapper job and 1 attempt successful as the entire job. I miss understanding how Rhipe works on compute notes to explain that.
2) when mapreduce.map.maxattempts=1 is set and job contains multiple mappers (say 300) then typically some small fraction of tasks begin to fall (with the same code 139) but later it stops and entire 300 completes successfully including new tasks that were started after failed one. Any idea?
I suspect 1 and 2 are related but don;t understand why.

Thanks again for quick and lively discussion.

Hi,

You're right, i dont need PATH (thought someone might and so the next version of RHIPE will have the fix i mentioned in the previous email).
My source script i load is now like this and most of these change will be pushed into RHIPE.

As for the 139 error, that's a segfault - it doesn't occur for me, so I can't quite help much here. However, does it occur /only/ for a few nodes?
Or is it randomly distributed across nodes , also does the error happen and not happen on the same node? is there something in common on the nodes
where it occurs?

Here my changes, which will be pushed into future versions of RHIPE (subject to everyone agreeing)

1. A version of ewrap which wraps boilerplate code around a  map.values etc
ewrap <- function(co1=NULL,before=NULL,after=NULL){
  co <- substitute(co1); before=substitute(before)
  j <- as.expression(bquote({
    .(BE)
    result <- mapply(function(.index,k,r){
      .(CO)
    },1:length(map.values),map.keys,map.values)
    .(AF)
  },list(CO=co,BE=before,AF=after)))
  class(j) <- c(class(j),"rhmr-map")
  j
}
So your code would look like ewrap({ do something with key=k, value=v}) ...

2.  file.types.remove.regex     ="(/_SUCCESS|/_LOG|/_log|rhipe\\.debug)"
I include .debug a feature in my version of  rhwatch

3. The templates also include max, min etc also, reducer expressions can have a 'combine' attribute set, which removes the need
specify combine=TRUE in rhmr (all the ones in rhoptions()$template will have it set)

3. rhwatch now has some debug stuff to it, e.g.
rhwatch(..., debug=c("count","stop","collect"))

in 'count', counters of R errors are displayed but the job is not killed - useful for those bad records
in 'stop': R errors cause it to stop
in 'collect',  the errors (some fraction of them) are written to rhipe.debug. files in the output folder and the errors are counted.
This Rdata files can be read for debugging purposes.

,debug                       = list( map=list(
                           setup=expression({
                             .errors <- as.environment(list(h=list(),maxcount=20))
                           }),
                           cleanup=expression({
                             if(length(.errors$h)>0){
                               save(.errors,file=sprintf("./tmp/rhipe_debug_%s",Sys.getenv("mapred.task.id <http://mapred.task.id>")))
                               rhcounter("@R_DebugFile","saved.files",1)
                             }})
                           ,handler=list(
                              count=function(e,k,r) rhcounter("R_UNTRAPPED_ERRORS",as.character(e),1)
                             ,"stop"=function(e,k,r) rhcounter("R_ERRORS",as.character(e),1)
                              ,collect=function(e,k,r){
                                if(length(.errors$h)<.errors$maxcount) {
                                  .errors$h <- append(.errors$h, list(list(error=e,map.value=r)))
                                  rhcounter("R_UNTRAPPED_ERRORS",e,1)
                                }
                              }
                              )

Thanks for your feedback on this.

Saptarshi

> 1. A version of ewrap which wraps boilerplate code around a  map.values etc
> ewrap <- function(co1=NULL,before=NULL,after=NULL){
>   co <- substitute(co1); before=substitute(before)
>   j <- as.expression(bquote({
>     .(BE)
>     result <- mapply(function(.index,k,r){
>       .(CO)
>     },1:length(map.values),map.keys,map.values)
>     .(AF)
>   },list(CO=co,BE=before,AF=after)))
>   class(j) <- c(class(j),"rhmr-map")
>   j
> }
> So your code would look like ewrap({ do something with key=k, value=v}) ...
>
> 2.  file.types.remove.regex     ="(/_SUCCESS|/_LOG|/_log|rhipe\\.debug)"
> I include .debug a feature in my version of  rhwatch
>
> 3. The templates also include max, min etc also, reducer expressions can have a 'combine' attribute set, which removes the need
> specify combine=TRUE in rhmr (all the ones in rhoptions()$template will have it set)
>
> 3. rhwatch now has some debug stuff to it, e.g.
> rhwatch(..., debug=c("count","stop","collect"))
>
> in 'count', counters of R errors are displayed but the job is not killed - useful for those bad records
> in 'stop': R errors cause it to stop
> in 'collect',  the errors (some fraction of them) are written to rhipe.debug. files in the output folder and the errors are counted.
> This Rdata files can be read for debugging purposes.
>
> ,debug                       = list( map=list(
>                            setup=expression({
>                              .errors <- as.environment(list(h=list(),maxcount=20))
>                            }),
>                            cleanup=expression({
>                              if(length(.errors$h)>0){
>                                save(.errors,file=sprintf("./tmp/rhipe_debug_%s",Sys.getenv("mapred.task.id <http://mapred.task.id>")))

>                                 if(length(.errors$h)<.errors$maxcount) {
